raw_response:
I've been working this land for 20 years. I know what Quzhou's soil and weather demand. My well gives me control over water that the rain doesn't always provide. With eight mouths to feed and a few of my kids earning wages off the farm, I don't need to gamble — I need steady cash from cotton and enough grain to keep the household fed without buying much.

**Cotton** is my main income. I'll put 8 mu into it. I plant in late April after the last frost risk. I buy improved seed from the county agri-supply store — not the most expensive hybrid, just the reliable local variety I've used for the past several years. I know how many times to irrigate from the well: four times through the season — at seedling, boll-setting, peak boll growth, and if August goes dry. I spray for bollworm and aphids based on what I see in the field, roughly five times. I deep-plough before planting because I've seen what compacted soil does to root development.

**Wheat and maize** share the same 6 mu. Wheat goes in October after I've cleared that ground. Maize follows right after the June wheat harvest. For maize I use hybrid seed — everyone around here switched to hybrid years ago and the yields are much better. I plant maize without ploughing again, just rotary tillage to break the wheat stubble.

I keep fertilizer at the levels I've used for years. I'm not experimenting at my age.
